title: Round 5 / ECDLP-15: cover-based transfers — genus/dimension trade-off (high-risk)
question: For E/F_p (p prime) and covers pi: C -> E of genus g with efficiently computable pullback pi^*: E(F_p) -> J_C(F_p), is there any regime of g (as a function of log p) where known Jacobian index-calculus complexities (Gaudry, Gaudry–Thomé–Thériault–Diem, Enge–Gaudry, Diem) applied to J_C beat sqrt(p)? Make the regime analysis rigorous from the published complexity statements (with exact hypotheses), and identify the precise missing ingredient; test the smallest case numerically if feasible.

claims: Proposition A (proved from cited statements): for fixed g>=2 or fixed plane degree d>=4 the cited index-calculus bounds on J_C(F_p) have exponent >=1 in q=p, hence exceed sqrt(p) for large p; no fixed-genus cover beats rho in the order-r subgroup.

Proposition B (proved from cited regimes; S6 regime is unverified recollection, S7 is heuristic): for g>=delta*log q the L_{q^g}(1/2,c) cost exceeds sqrt(q) for all large q; for g>=(log q)^2 the L_{q^g}(1/3,c) cost exceeds sqrt(q) for large q.

Proposition C (heuristic, derived): generic degree-1 factor-base index calculus on a genus-g Jacobian costs >= about q/20 for 1<=g<=sqrt(q), so the L-formulas are not applicable below their validity regimes.

Lemma D (elementary): pull-back relations pi^*(P)=sum of fibre places have disjoint supports over distinct P and determine no individual factor-base logarithm; toy numerics show the relation/unknown ratio is about 1/d.

Prime fields have no Weil descent; the GHS/Gaudry/Diem gains for E/F_{q^n} (n>=2) come from the smaller base field and do not transfer. Cover E x_{P^1} P^1 by t->t^d has genus (3d-1)/2 (d odd) or (3d-2)/2 (d even); generic h gives 2d-1.
Missing ingredient: a structure-adapted factor base of size <=p^{1/2-eps} with fast decomposition of elements of pi^*(E(F_p)) in J_C; none known.
next_action: PI to review Propositions A-C and the unverified items (Gaudry 2000 exponent, Enge-Gaudry regime). Optional T2: run genus-2 index calculus on J_C = E x E_2 for p~2^20 to confirm cost >= p vs rho 2^10 on E. Close this direction unless a structure-adapted factor base (4.2 item II-III) is proposed.
